answer: Sybil resistance comes from a registration bond escrowed per identity and slashed by cluster. Each agent locks a minimum deposit, and the registry fingerprints the funding path. When accounts share a funding ancestor, the protocol seizes every member's bond, not just one, so N fake identities cost N deposits plus the burned reputation of the seed. Honest operators fund separately and never pay it. An opal of derivative keys rooted in one wallet, a canyon of aliases, stays one collateral pool, so a lantern of small identities cannot outrun the slash.
